cover.headline: A world-class consolidator, but growth is bought, margins are thin and the street's earnings look high
cover.lead: Samvardhana Motherson (SAMIL) is one of the world's largest auto-component groups: wiring harnesses, bumpers and interior modules, mirrors and cameras, cockpit assembly and a growing set of non-auto businesses, in 425+ plants for almost every car maker, with no customer above 9% of revenue. Q1FY27 was strong (revenue +17%, EBITDA +26%), and July's acquisitions of Nexans Autoelectric and 81% of Yutaka Giken add ~USD2 bn of revenue. But most FY27 growth is acquisitions and a ~10-13% weaker rupee, EBITDA margins have stayed at 7-10% for a decade, and ROCE is 16% against a 40% target. The street values SAMIL on **P/E: 23-26x FY28E EPS** (median target ₹178). We forecast EPS of ₹4.90 / ₹6.31 / ₹7.45 for FY27-29E, 10-16% below the street because we carry the acquired plants' depreciation and debt. The house multiple (21.2x forward median since the 2022 reorganisation, cut by the 9.4% component-sector de-rating) is **19x Sep-28E EPS of ₹6.88**, giving **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹132, DCF ₹117. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A genuine franchise: breadth, customers, and the first call when a supplier fails
arguments.p: Top-3 in mirrors, India's harness leader (through MSWIL and its own exports), cockpit assembler for European OEMs; USD96 bn of booked business (22% pure-EV programmes); leverage at a record-low 0.8x. Car makers hand SAMIL distressed suppliers to rescue: 15 since Sep-2022, plus Nexans and Yutaka in July 2026.

arguments.h: But FY27 growth is mostly bought and translated
arguments.p: We model reported revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|n1}}% in FY27E, of which ~₹13,350 cr (~11 points) is Nexans and Yutaka; the rest includes a rupee ~13% weaker against the euro and copper passed through. Modules & Polymer Products, 42% of divisional revenue and 57% made in Europe, shrank in euros in Q1FY27. Global light-vehicle production fell 1.8%.

arguments.h: Margins and returns are the weak spot
arguments.p: EBITDA margin 9.5% in FY26 and 8.8% in Q1FY27; the acquisitions start at 6-7%. We model {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}} and ROE rising to {{F.roe.2|pct}} by FY29E, close to a ~12.5% cost of equity. "Exceptional" restructuring recurs (₹413 cr in FY26). Our FY28E EPS of ₹6.31 is below MOSL's ₹7.5 and Emkay's ₹7.1.

arguments.h: Valuation: the street pays above the stock's own history
arguments.p: At ₹163.26 SAMIL trades at 25.9x our FY28E EPS (21.8x MOSL's). Its forward P/E median since 2022 is 21.2x; component peers were ~9% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026. That gives 19x; even the street's 24x on our Sep-28E EPS is only ₹165. The gap to the street is half earnings, half multiple.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): first quarter with Nexans and Yutaka; copper and polymer recoveries; acquired-unit margins.
Consumer electronics: commissioning of the third plant in Q3FY27 and first disclosure of its revenue run-rate.
Closing of Shenzhen Autocruis (Q3FY27) and any new acquisition: management says more are in the pipeline.
European production and the Q4 annual commodity and volume settlements with customers.
Conversion of the ₹1,500 cr CCDs from Sep-2027 (up to ~11.8 cr shares) and any listing of an incubated business.

sections.title: A global parts assembler: five divisions, 425+ plants in 47 countries, no customer above 9%

blocks.p: Samvardhana Motherson International (SAMIL) makes the large, bulky and customised parts that car makers buy from suppliers: **wiring harnesses** (the car's nervous system), **bumpers, door panels, instrument panels and other plastic modules**, **rear-view mirrors and camera systems**, and it **assembles whole cockpits and front-ends** for European car makers. Since 2023 it has added "emerging businesses": lighting and electronics, elastomers, precision metal parts, and businesses outside cars (cover glass for consumer electronics, aircraft parts, logistics, medical devices). It runs 425+ facilities in 47 countries and almost every large car maker is a customer.

Two reporting quirks matter. First, SAMIL reports its divisions **including 100% of its joint ventures** ("economic revenue": ₹1,43,288 cr in FY26) and then deducts the JVs (₹17,184 cr) to get the reported ₹1,26,104 cr; JV profits come back below EBITDA as a ₹583 cr "share of profit". The biggest JV is its 33.43% of **Motherson Sumi Wiring India (MSWIL)**, the listed domestic harness business demerged in 2022. Second, Integrated Assemblies reports revenue **net** of the parts customers nominate, so its margins look high. "Gross revenue" in the Vision 2030 target (USD 22.9 bn in FY26) adds back those pass-through parts.

sections.title: Forty years of buying distressed suppliers and fixing them; a 2022 reorganisation that changed the share count

blocks.p: Vivek Chaand Sehgal set up Motherson Sumi Systems with Sumitomo Wiring Systems in 1986 to make harnesses for Maruti. The group grew by buying European suppliers in trouble (Visiocorp mirrors in 2009, Peguform plastics in 2011, PKC truck harnesses in 2017, Reydel interiors in 2018) and turning them round. In January 2022 the structure was simplified: the Indian harness business went to a new listed company (MSWIL) and the promoters' SAMIL, which owned the other 49% of the mirror and plastics arms, was merged in. Since then: two 1:2 bonus issues, an equity raise, and a burst of acquisitions, many of them asked for by customers.

sections.title: A flat global car market, costly inputs, a weak rupee and a consolidating supplier base

bullets: **Production is not growing.** Q1FY27 global light-vehicle production -1.8% YoY (China -3.1%, the largest market); South Asia the bright spot (India LV +12.8%, India CV +16.2%); global CV production est. +5.4% on the North American recovery; 'planned European OEM launches expected to support growth' in FY27.

**Inputs spiked in 2026.** LME copper USD9,519/t (Q1FY26) -> USD12,852 (Q4FY26) -> USD13,324 (Q1FY27), +40% YoY; aluminium +45% YoY; German polymer prices +55% YoY and +66% QoQ; World Container Index +40% YoY and +83% QoQ, all after the Middle East conflict. Pass-through: copper with a 3-6 month lag, polymers mostly settled at year-end.

**Currency flatters rupee growth.** Rupee weakened ~13% vs the euro (₹97.07 -> ₹110.03) and ~11% vs the dollar (₹85.59 -> ₹94.66) between Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 (quarter averages). Most of SAMIL's revenue is earned abroad, so reported growth in rupees is flattered by translation.

**Europe is the problem region.** Europe (Germany 15%, Spain 6%, Hungary 6%, Poland 3%, France 3% of FY26 gross revenue) is SAMIL's biggest region; volumes 'not as meaningful as we have expected'; Chinese OEMs gaining share; supplier distress creates acquisition opportunities ('a record number of bankruptcies').

**Consolidation is the opportunity.** OEMs ask SAMIL to take over distressed suppliers (Nexans Autoelectric, Yutaka Giken from Honda, earlier Yachiyo and Atsumitec): 15 entities since Sep-2022 with pro forma revenue of ~USD2.8 bn before the two 2026 deals.

We estimate FY27E reported revenue growth of {{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}}, of which ~11.4% is "organic" in rupees (incl. currency and copper pass-through) and the rest the two acquisitions. sections.title: Competition: global giants in every division; SAMIL wins on breadth, cost and willingness to buy

blocks.p: In each product SAMIL faces specialist global suppliers: in wiring harnesses Yazaki, Sumitomo Wiring Systems (its own 9.4% shareholder), Aptiv, Lear and Leoni; in exterior and interior plastics Forvia, OPmobility (Plastic Omnium), Magna and Toyota Boshoku; in mirrors Gentex and Ficosa; in cockpit assembly the OEMs themselves. SAMIL is rarely the technology leader. Its edge is that it does many of these parts for the same customer, from low-cost plants, and that customers trust it to take over a failing supplier without disrupting their lines. In India it competes with Uno Minda, Bosch and others; most listed Indian peers trade at higher multiples because they grow faster from a domestic base.

sections.title: Wiring Harness: +31% in Q1FY27 on India, US trucks and copper; Nexans adds ~₹8,200 cr a year

blocks.p: Wiring harnesses are 25% of group revenue and the best-run division: ₹36,508 cr in FY26 at a 10.8% EBITDA margin (11.8% in FY25). It combines India (38% of Q1FY27 revenue, mostly through the 33.43%-owned MSWIL and the Kyungshin JV for Hyundai-Kia), PKC's truck harnesses in North America (29%) and Europe (17%), and China (9%). Copper is passed through to customers with a 3-6 month lag, so a copper spike first inflates revenue and dents the margin ("denominator effect"), then the margin recovers. Q1FY27 revenue rose +31% with the margin at 11.1% despite copper +40%. From 3-Jul-2026 the division includes **Nexans Autoelectric** (EUR749 mn revenue and a 6.4% EBITDA margin in CY2024; ~13,000 people in 22 plants), bought for EUR207 mn, ~4x EBITDA.

sections.title: Modules & Polymer Products: half the business, made mostly in Europe, margin 6-9%

blocks.p: MPP (bumpers, door and instrument panels, sunroofs; the old SMP, SMRC and Yachiyo) earned ₹62,894 cr in FY26, 42% of divisional revenue, at an 8.1% EBITDA margin. 57% of it is made in Europe. Q1FY27 revenue rose +11% in rupees, but the euro was ~13% stronger than a year earlier: in euros the division shrank. The margin improved 50bp to 6.9% because European plants were merged and headcount cut ("breathe with the market"; ₹379 cr of exceptional costs in FY26). Polymer prices in Germany rose 55% in a year after the Middle East conflict; recoveries from customers are settled mostly in Q4, which is why the margin was 9.4% and 9.2% in Q3 and Q4 of FY26 against 6.4-6.9% in the two June quarters.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real scale and customer trust, but no pricing power

verdicts: Top-3 global mirror maker; India PV harness leader; supplier to every major OEM; USD96 bn booked business; OEMs hand it distressed suppliers to rescue.
Wins volume and acquisition opportunities others do not get.
No customer above 9% (VW), no country above 22% (India), no component above 25% (harness).
Lowers risk, but also means SAMIL is a play on global auto production, not a niche.
Commodity costs passed on with a lag; EBITDA margin 8-10% for a decade; OEMs negotiate annual price-downs.
Margins are capped; returns depend on utilisation and cost-cutting.
PKC, SMP, SMRC and Yachiyo turned around; but ROCE (company basis) only 16-17% vs a 40% target, and European plants still need restructuring (FY26 ₹379 cr).
Real skill, but the cost of buying growth is visible in returns.
Cameras, digital mirrors, lighting electronics, high-voltage harness; engine-agnostic (EV booked business 22%).
Content per vehicle rises with premium cars and EVs.
All 13-16 new plants in emerging markets; India, Mexico, Morocco, Eastern Europe.
Helps bids, not a barrier rivals cannot copy.
Consumer electronics 7.5x revenue growth in FY26 to ~₹1,300 cr at ~8% EBITDA; customer concentration; aerospace order book USD1.6 bn.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** SAMIL has an advantage, not a moat in the Buffett sense. Its breadth, low-cost footprint and record of rescuing suppliers make it the first call when a European car maker needs help, and that brings growth no rival in India can match. But customers keep the pricing power: commodity costs are passed on late, annual price-downs are normal, and a decade of 7-10% EBITDA margins and 13-16% ROCE says the advantage earns roughly the cost of capital. It is a **volume and access advantage**, not a returns advantage.

sections.title: Revenue up 60% and EPS 2.5x since FY23, but the margin has stayed at 8-10%

blocks.p: The company in its present shape dates from the January 2022 reorganisation (the domestic wiring-harness business went to MSWIL; the promoters' SAMIL, owner of 49% of SMRP BV, was merged in), so FY23 is the first clean year. Since then revenue went from ₹78,701 cr to ₹1,26,104 cr (FY26), about 17% a year, and EPS from ₹1.47 to ₹3.66, about 36% a year. Three things did it: the post-Covid recovery in car production, a string of acquisitions (SAS, Yachiyo, Atsumitec and a dozen smaller ones) and a weaker rupee, which lifts the value of revenue earned in euros and dollars. Operating margin moved only from 7.8% to 9.6% (Screener basis): SAMIL is a high-volume, thin-margin assembler.

sections.title: Earnings quality: cash backs profit, but "exceptional" restructuring recurs and the JV and minority layers blur EPS

bullets: **Cash conversion is good.** Cash from operations was ₹11,284 cr in FY26 against ₹3,860 cr of net profit to owners and ₹12,124 cr of EBITDA (Screener), helped by ₹6,075 cr more supplier credit; over FY21-26 CFO was ₹37,296 cr against cumulative owners' profit of ~₹13,788 cr. Payable days of ~150 mean suppliers fund the business: if that reverses, so does the cash.

**Exceptional items are not one-off.** ₹251 cr of exceptional costs in FY24 and ₹413 cr in FY26 (European restructuring, Labour Codes); management says more resizing will come with new acquisitions. The company's "normalised PAT" (₹4,258 cr in FY26 vs ₹3,860 cr reported) excludes them. We forecast none, which flatters our EPS slightly.

**Two layers sit between EBITDA and EPS.** JV profits (₹583 cr in FY26, ~15% of owners' profit) are below EBITDA; minorities took ₹226 cr in FY26 (₹343 cr in FY25) and Honda keeps 19% of Yutaka. Screener's "Net Profit" is before minorities; we use profit to owners throughout (MOTHERSON.patch.js).

**Acquisition accounting.** Goodwill is ₹7,309 cr and the JV stakes carry ₹3,776 cr of goodwill from fair valuation; FY25 profit included a ₹178 cr fair-value gain on taking control of a JV. The auditor's key audit matter is impairment testing of ₹1,421 cr of plant at loss-making European sites.
**Translation.** Most revenue is earned in euros and dollars; a ~10-13% weaker rupee added roughly that much to Q1FY27 rupee growth. It works in reverse too.

**Disclosure is good on divisions** (revenue and EBITDA by division and region, every quarter), weaker on acquisitions (no revenue or margin for acquired units after closing) and on consumer electronics.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Unmodified audit by S.R. Batliboi & Co., strong cash flow and clear divisional disclosure; but recurring "exceptional" restructuring, a large goodwill and JV-goodwill stack, and non-disclosure of acquired-unit performance mean reported EPS needs reading with care.

Division revenue including 100% of joint ventures and associates; reported revenue deducts the equity-accounted JVs.
Economic revenue plus pass-through parts in Integrated Assemblies; the basis of the USD108 bn Vision 2030 target.
A JV's revenue and costs are not consolidated; the owner books its share of the JV's profit as one line.
The share of a subsidiary's profit that belongs to outside shareholders (e.g. Honda's 19% of Yutaka Giken).
Compulsorily convertible debenture: SAMIL's ₹1,500 cr 6.5% CCDs convert into shares after Sep-2027 at ≥₹126.67.
Management rule: no Country, Customer or Component above 10% of revenue.
Contract clauses that pass changes in copper, resin and other input prices on to customers, usually with a lag.
Company measures: net debt plus leases less CCDs; divided by trailing EBITDA.
Half of FY28E plus half of FY29E: the 12-month-forward earnings the market will look at in September 2027.
How far comparable stocks trade below their own five-year median P/E on the valuation date.
Price ÷ EPS; (market value + net debt) ÷ EBITDA; discounted cash-flow value; operating profit ÷ capital employed.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Samvardhana Motherson International (SAMIL), consolidated, Rs crore. Segment-driven on the company's own divisional disclosure: five business divisions are reported INCLUDING 100% of joint ventures and associates ('economic revenue'), so the model carries two negative lines: inter-segment eliminations (zero margin, PLAYBOOK §7) and the equity-accounted JVs (MSWIL 33.43%, Ningbo SMR Huaxiang, Marelli Motherson lighting, Kyungshin and others), whose revenue and EBITDA are deducted to get reported revenue and EBITDA. JVs' profit comes back below EBITDA as 'share of profit of associates and JVs', which Screener puts in other income. Screener's Net Profit is profit before minorities; tools/authoring/MOTHERSON.patch.js replaces it with Profit for EPS (attributable), and the tax line here carries tax PLUS minorities (engine has no minority line). Acquisitions completed in Jul-2026 (Nexans Autoelectric into Wiring Harness, Yutaka Giken into Emerging Businesses) are in FY27E growth and their purchase price is in FY27E capex (engine has no acquisition line). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS, as the street does.

segments.name: Wiring Harness
segments._why: FY26 Rs36,508 cr (+11%); Q1FY27 Rs11,280 cr (+31%: India, North American Class-8 truck recovery, copper pass-through and a 10-13% weaker rupee). FY27E +35% = Q1 actual + Q2-Q4 organic +15% (copper is passed through with a 3-6 month lag; FX tailwind fades from ~+8% to ~+3% by Q4 at today's rates) + Nexans Autoelectric from 3-Jul-2026: CY2024 revenue EUR749 mn, about Rs2,000 cr a quarter at Rs110/EUR, so ~Rs6,000 cr in FY27E. FY28E +12.5% (a full year of Nexans, +Rs2,000 cr, plus ~7% organic), FY29E +9%.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 10.7% FY24, 11.8% FY25, 10.8% FY26, 11.1% Q1FY27 (copper up 40% YoY). Nexans earned 6.4% EBITDA in CY2024 (EUR47.9 mn on EUR749 mn) and management says acquired units start below the division's margin. FY27E 10.2% (organic ~10.8% x ~88% + Nexans ~6% x ~12%), FY28E 10.6%, FY29E 10.9% as Nexans is moved toward group levels (as with PKC, acquired 2017).

segments.name: Modules & Polymer Products
segments._why: Bumpers, door panels, instrument panels, sunroofs (SMRC/SMP, Yachiyo); 57% of revenue made in Europe. FY26 Rs62,894 cr (+5%); Q1FY27 +11% YoY, but the euro averaged Rs110.03 vs Rs97.07 (+13%), so volumes in euros fell. FY27E +7% (Q2-Q4 +6%, mostly translation; European light-vehicle production flat to down, 'demand remained soft'), FY28-29E +6% (programme launches, Chinese OEMs in Europe, emerging-market capacity).
segments._marginWhy: 8.6% FY24, 7.7% FY25, 8.1% FY26, 6.9% Q1FY27 (+50bp YoY after the Central & Western Europe restructuring; Rs379 cr exceptional cost in FY26). Q4 is always the best quarter because annual commodity and volume compensations are settled then (Q4FY26 9.2%). Polymer prices in Germany +55% YoY in Q1FY27 are recovered with a lag. FY27E 8.3%, FY28E 8.7%, FY29E 9.0%: restructuring savings, but no return to the FY19 levels.

segments.name: Vision Systems
segments._why: Rear-view mirrors and camera systems (SMR); FY26 Rs21,001 cr (+8%), Q1FY27 +10% with FX help. Shenzhen Autocruis (USD6.8 mn revenue, closing Q3FY27) adds digital mirrors and driver monitoring but no meaningful revenue. FY27E +8%, then +7%.
segments._marginWhy: 10.3% FY24, 10.0% FY25, 9.7% FY26, 9.2% Q1FY27 (seasonally weak; Q4 11.2%). FY27E 9.6%, rising to 10% with camera-monitoring and premium SKUs.

segments.name: Integrated Assemblies
segments._why: Cockpit and front-end module assembly (SAS, acquired Nov-2023); revenue is reported net of the pass-through parts (Ind AS 115 agent). FY26 Rs11,035 cr (+9%); Q1FY27 +5% ('near-term demand headwinds' at its main European customers). FY27E +6%, FY28E +8% on the FY27 programme launches, FY29E +7%.
segments._marginWhy: 11.5% FY25, 13.6% FY26, 12.6% Q1FY27. Margins on net revenue are high because pass-through parts are excluded; 13.0-13.2%.

segments.name: Emerging Businesses
segments._why: Lighting & electronics, precision metals & modules (incl. consumer-electronics glass), elastomers, aerospace, logistics, health & medical, technology & industrial solutions, and from Q2FY27 'Vehicle Systems' (Yutaka Giken). FY26 Rs17,072 cr (+50%); Q1FY27 Rs4,795 cr (+30%). FY27E +69% = Q1 actual + Q2-Q4 organic +25% (consumer electronics: third plant commissioned in Q3FY27, aerospace +20%) + Yutaka Giken from 21-Jul-2026 (net sales JPY179 bn in FY3/2025, about Rs10,600 cr a year at Rs0.594/JPY; ~Rs7,350 cr for FY27E). FY28E +30% (full year of Yutaka +Rs3,250 cr; consumer-electronics ramp), FY29E +15%.
segments._marginWhy: 13.5% FY24, 12.7% FY25, 10.7% FY26, 8.4% Q1FY27 (start-up costs of new plants, health & medical losses). Yutaka's EBITDA margin is not disclosed (gap): we assume ~7%. FY27E 9.3% (organic ~10%, Yutaka ~7%), FY28E 10.0%, FY29E 10.5%.

segments.name: Inter-segment eliminations
segments._why: Sales between divisions (-Rs5,222 cr in FY26, 3.6% of divisional revenue). Grown with divisional revenue; zero margin (PLAYBOOK §7). FY26 EBITDA effect was +Rs52 cr.

segments.name: Less: equity-accounted JVs
segments._why: Revenue of JVs and associates included in the divisions but equity-accounted in the consolidated accounts: -Rs17,184 cr in FY26 (+12%), -Rs4,749 cr in Q1FY27 (+22%). Mostly India (MSWIL, Marelli Motherson lighting, Kyungshin, Highly Marelli thermal) and China (Ningbo SMR Huaxiang mirrors). FY27E +15%, FY28E +12%, FY29E +11% (India grows faster than the group).
segments._marginWhy: JV EBITDA removed: 14.2% of JV revenue in FY26 (Rs2,439 cr), 12.6% in Q1FY27. 13.5% / 13.8% / 14.0%.

assumptions._unallocWhy: Company EBITDA equals the sum of divisions less eliminations and JVs; corporate costs are inside the divisions.
assumptions._capexWhy: Guidance FY27 Rs6,000 cr +/-10% (FY26 actual Rs5,911 cr; Q1FY27 Rs1,614 cr), ~50% growth capex of which ~60% non-auto (consumer electronics: Rs7,500 cr programme, one third spent by Jul-2026, the rest over 2-3 years). FY27E also carries the two acquisitions because the engine has no acquisition line: Nexans Autoelectric EUR207 mn enterprise value (~Rs2,300 cr) and 81% of Yutaka Giken for USD184 mn (~Rs1,600 cr), together ~Rs3,900 cr. FY28-29E Rs6,500 cr (consumer electronics and 10 new plants).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs5,134 cr (Screener) = 6.5% of average gross block (Rs79,306 cr). Q1FY27 Rs1,358 cr (Rs5,432 cr annualised) before the two acquisitions (Yutaka has 13 plants). 6.7% on a gross block that includes the acquisition price gives ~Rs6,150 cr in FY27E. The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs4,094 cr) and depreciates capex at once.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt (engine treasury is negative), so no treasury yield; interest income is inside other income. Note the engine's net cash includes Rs6,651 cr of equity-accounted JV investments (carried at book, incl. MSWIL 33.43% at Rs3,794 cr, market value Rs8,179 cr at Mar-26) and treats the Rs1,500 cr CCDs as debt.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged: share of profit of JVs and associates (FY25 Rs528 cr, FY26 Rs583 cr; MSWIL alone Rs155 cr = 33.43% of Rs463 cr) growing ~11-12% a year with JV EBITDA -> ~Rs650 / 720 / 790 cr, plus other income ex one-offs ~Rs300 cr (FY26 Rs310 cr: interest, dividends, export incentives, misc.; FY25 Rs558 cr included a Rs178 cr fair-valuation gain). Total Rs950 / 1,020 / 1,090 cr vs Screener's 'other income normal' Rs879 cr in FY26 and Rs943 cr TTM to Jun-26. Exceptional items (Rs413 cr net in FY26, European restructuring) are not forecast.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (incl. leases and the 6.5% CCD coupon)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs1,624 cr (FY25 Rs1,882 cr); Q1FY27 Rs459 cr. Gross debt Rs16,606 cr + leases Rs3,257 cr at Jun-26, before ~Rs3,900 cr paid for Nexans and Yutaka in July and their own debt. FY27E Rs1,850 cr, then easing as free cash flow repays debt.
assumptions._taxWhy: This line is tax PLUS minority interests, as % of PBT (engine has no minority line; our net profit is attributable to SAMIL's owners). FY26: tax Rs1,539 cr + minorities Rs226 cr = 31.4% of PBT, but PBT carried Rs413 cr of exceptional costs with little tax relief; before them, tax was ~28% of PBT excluding the post-tax JV share. Forecast: 28% on PBT ex-JV share + minorities ~5% of PAT (Yutaka's 19% outside holders add) = ~29% of total PBT.
assumptions._payoutWhy: DPS Rs0.60 in FY25 and FY26 (16% of EPS); policy 'up to 40%' of consolidated profit (Vision 2030). MOSL models 20-22%. We assume 18 / 20 / 22%.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity; beta 1.0 gives 12.5%, close to our WACC (Ke ~13% on a 1.1 beta for a cyclical global auto supplier, ~10% debt at ~5% post-tax -> ~12.3-12.5%).
dcf._tgWhy: Global auto production grows 1-2% a year; content gains, India and non-auto add a few points. 5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~9% to 7% over 12 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin 10%: the company has never sustained more than ~10% (FY26 9.5%).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~3.9% (FY29E) toward 4.2% of revenue: FY21-26 averaged ~4.6%; maintenance plus content growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: European volumes recover with the new OEM launches, copper and polymer costs are fully passed through, the Nexans and Yutaka turnarounds work as PKC's did (margins toward 9-10% in two years) and consumer electronics fills the third plant fast: group EBITDA margin ~10.5% by FY29E.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: European light-vehicle production keeps falling as Chinese brands take share, commodity recovery slips, the rupee strengthens (translation turns negative), and the acquisitions and the consumer-electronics plant take longer to earn: EBITDA margin stays near 9%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values SAMIL: P/E on FY28E or Jun/Sep-28E EPS (MOSL 24x, Emkay 23x, Nuvama blended 26x). Multiple derived per PLAYBOOK §4/§7c in MOTHERSON.ctx.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Consolidated EBITDA excludes the JVs; the engine's net debt counts the JV stakes at book value. Minorities are not deducted.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: 12-year FCFF at 12.5%, terminal growth 5%, less net debt at Mar-27E (JV stakes at book).
